deck_context.source_summary: Based mainly on Hugging Face's article about assisted generation, with the original speculative decoding paper used for credibility. The core mechanism is simple: a smaller draft model proposes several tokens quickly, and the larger target model verifies them, accepting correct guesses and replacing the first wrong guess.
deck_context.core_claim: Speculative decoding speeds up text generation by letting a fast helper model draft tokens while the large model still controls the final output.
deck_context.speaker_split: Speaker 1 covers slides 1-3, Speaker 2 covers slides 4-6, Speaker 3 covers slides 7-9, and Speaker 4 covers slides 10-12.

slides.title: The Problem: One Piece at a Time
slides.intent: Explain token-by-token generation before introducing the speedup.
key_points: Large language models write text step by step.
Each next token needs another model step.
Many repeated steps create waiting time.

slides.title: The Core Idea
slides.intent: Introduce assisted generation as draft, verify, answer.
key_points: A small model quickly drafts several next tokens.
A large model checks the draft.
The large model still controls the final answer.

slides.title: Draft Model vs Target Model
slides.intent: Clarify the two model roles without suggesting the small model replaces the large one.
key_points: The draft model is smaller and faster.
The target model is larger and more reliable.
They work as a team, not replacements.
slides.speaker_focus: Speaker 2 contrasts the helper role with the decision-maker role.

slides.title: Speculative Decoding
slides.intent: Approved sample slide showing the draft-and-verify workflow with a concrete token example.
key_points: The small model guesses several tokens first.
The large model verifies the guessed tokens together.
Accepted guesses move forward; a wrong guess is replaced.
slides.speaker_focus: Speaker 3 walks through the sample: prompt, draft tokens, verification, accepted tokens, rejected token, and replacement.

local_context.required_background: Use the approved concrete example: prompt 'Today I ate a', draft tokens 'slice', 'of', 'pizza', 'yesterday', accepted tokens 'slice', 'of', 'pizza', rejected draft 'yesterday', replacement token 'for'.

constraints: This slide is already approved and should not be regenerated.

slides.title: Does It Hurt Quality?
slides.intent: Answer the main audience concern about whether speed sacrifices correctness.
key_points: The small model only suggests.
The large model accepts good guesses and rejects bad ones.
The final output can preserve the large model's behavior.
slides.speaker_focus: Speaker 3 explains that the target model remains in control.

local_context.required_background: Avoid overstating. Say that in the standard method, verification is designed so the target model controls the output distribution.

slides.title: When It Works Best
slides.intent: Explain the conditions for speedup and avoid overclaiming.
key_points: The draft model must be much faster than the large model.
